memo.summary: Subject 101-9001 received a double dose of Study Drug XJ-401 at Visit 3 (Week 8), constituting a major protocol deviation from the specified dosing regimen. This has been classified as an important protocol deviation requiring expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation resulted from an administration error during Visit 3 dosing, in which the subject received twice the protocol-specified dose of XJ-401. The classifier's initial categorization of 'major' was confirmed on adjudication with high confidence (0.92) and was not overridden. No site-history pattern of similar dosing errors was noted in the materials provided; root cause appears isolated to this administration event pending further site-level investigation into dispensing/verification procedures at the time of dosing.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation defined per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain site dosing/dispensing staff specifically on the dual-verification step for dose calculation and administration of XJ-401, with emphasis on Visit 3 dosing procedures.
Conduct a clinical reassessment of Subject 101-9001, including safety monitoring for adverse effects related to the double dose, and document findings in the subject's medical record and study file.

Implement an added monitoring checkpoint requiring a second independent staff member to verify dose volume/quantity against the dosing log prior to administration for all subsequent visits at this site.
Perform a site-level review of dosing records for other enrolled subjects to confirm no similar undetected dosing errors have occurred.
Submit expedited deviation report to IRB and sponsor per required timelines, including corrective action summary.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator (in coordination with Site Study Coordinator and Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 calendar days of deviation identification, pending human quality reviewer confirmation

memo.summary: Subject 102-9002 was enrolled into the trial despite failing to meet the renal function exclusion criterion, indicating a screening eligibility review failure. Classified as a major/important protocol deviation.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The screening process at the site failed to correctly identify that the subject's renal function value fell outside the protocol-specified eligible range, resulting in enrollment of an ineligible subject. This suggests a breakdown in the eligibility verification step during screening, either due to inadequate cross-checking of lab values against exclusion criteria or insufficient staff review prior to enrollment sign-off. No site-history pattern or classifier override was noted in the adjudication record for this event; classification remained consistent as major.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); base deviation definition per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain screening/enrollment staff at the site specifically on verifying renal function exclusion criteria against lab reference ranges prior to enrollment sign-off

Conduct a clinical reassessment of Subject 102-9002's current renal function and evaluate continued eligibility, safety monitoring needs, or potential discontinuation per protocol and medical monitor input
Implement an added eligibility checkpoint requiring independent second-person verification of all exclusion-criterion lab values before enrollment confirmation is finalized
Perform a retrospective review of recently screened/enrolled subjects at this site to confirm no similar renal function eligibility errors occurred
Report the deviation to the IRB and sponsor per expedited reporting timelines given its classification as a major/important deviation
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator, in coordination with Site Clinical Research Coordinator and Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs team
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 calendar days of memo issuance, pending human reviewer confirmation

memo.summary: Subject 103-9003 underwent a protocol-mandated biopsy prior to obtaining written informed consent, constituting a major protocol deviation involving a breach of subject rights and consent safeguards.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The site proceeded with an invasive, protocol-mandated procedure before executing written informed consent, indicating a breakdown in the site's consent verification process ahead of scheduling or performing invasive study procedures. The classifier's initial 'major' categorization was confirmed on adjudication (not overridden), consistent with this being a consent-process failure involving direct subject impact. No prior site-history pattern was provided in the materials reviewed; if repeat consent-timing issues exist at this site, they should be flagged during investigation and addressed in the CAPA scope.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation definition per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain site staff involved in the biopsy scheduling/consent workflow on the requirement that written informed consent must be fully executed and documented before any protocol-mandated invasive procedure is initiated

Conduct a reassessment of Subject 103-9003, including documentation of a post-hoc informed consent discussion, evaluation of whether the subject wishes to continue participation, and clinical review of any biopsy-related risk or harm incurred prior to consent

Implement a pre-procedure checklist/sign-off step requiring verification of a signed consent form in the subject's file before any invasive study procedure (e.g., biopsy) can be scheduled or performed
Conduct a site-level chart review of other subjects who underwent invasive procedures to confirm consent was properly obtained beforehand, to rule out a broader pattern
Report the deviation to the IRB and sponsor on an expedited basis per protocol and regulatory timelines
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator, in coordination with Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs and Clinical Quality Assurance
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 calendar days of this memo's issuance, pending human quality reviewer confirmation

memo.summary: Subject 104-9004 was inadvertently unblinded to site staff due to a randomization system error, constituting a major protocol deviation involving loss of treatment assignment concealment.
memo.root_cause_narrative: An error within the randomization system resulted in disclosure of Subject 104-9004's treatment assignment to site staff, indicating a failure of the technical or procedural safeguard designed to maintain blinding. The classifier's initial 'major' categorization was confirmed on adjudication without override, supporting that this is a significant deviation with potential impact on data integrity and subject/study bias. No site-history pattern of similar unblinding events was noted in the materials provided, but the root cause appears to be a system-level control failure rather than an isolated human error, warranting review of the randomization system's design and access controls.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation classified per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Conduct a technical root-cause investigation of the randomization system to identify the specific error mechanism that led to disclosure of Subject 104-9004's treatment assignment, and implement a system fix or patch to prevent recurrence.
Retrain site staff involved in randomization and blinding procedures on proper handling of randomization system outputs and escalation steps if an unblinding event is suspected.

Assess Subject 104-9004's continued participation and data validity in light of the unblinding, including consultation with the medical monitor/biostatistician on whether the subject's data should be flagged, excluded from primary analysis, or handled per a pre-specified unblinding contingency plan.

Implement an added monitoring checkpoint, such as an automated alert or dual-verification step within the randomization system, to detect and block similar unblinding errors before they reach site staff.
Notify the IRB and sponsor per expedited reporting timelines and document the unblinding event and corrective actions in the trial master file.
Review randomization logs across the site (and other sites using the same system) for evidence of similar near-misses or a recurring pattern.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator, in coordination with Sponsor's Safety/Regulatory Affairs team and the randomization system vendor
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 calendar days of this memo (expedited due to unblinding impact on data integrity)

memo.summary: A temperature excursion in the Site 105 storage freezer went undetected prior to dispensing, resulting in Subject 105-9005 receiving out-of-spec drug product and subsequently experiencing an adverse reaction consistent with the dosing error. This is classified as a major protocol deviation with subject safety impact.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The root cause is a breakdown in the temperature monitoring and dispensing-release safeguard at Site 105: the freezer excursion was not identified or flagged before the affected product was released for dosing, indicating either a gap in continuous temperature monitoring/alarm response or a failure to verify temperature logs against the accepted range prior to dispensing. This failure directly led to administration of out-of-spec product and a resulting adverse reaction in the subject. The classifier's initial category (major) was retained without override, and no prior site-history pattern was noted in the materials provided, though given the direct subject harm, site-level monitoring practices should be reviewed for recurrence risk.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation defined per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain Site 105 pharmacy/dispensing staff specifically on the freezer temperature-check and release-verification step that must be completed before any product is dispensed, including documentation of sign-off against the temperature log.

Conduct a clinical reassessment of Subject 105-9005, including review of the adverse reaction, causality assessment, and any needed medical follow-up or treatment related to receipt of out-of-spec product.

Implement an added checkpoint requiring a second-person verification (or automated temperature-excursion alert lockout) that blocks dispensing of any product stored in a freezer with an unresolved or unreviewed excursion flag.

Audit freezer temperature logs and dispensing records at Site 105 for the preceding monitoring period to identify any other subjects who may have received product from the same or other excursion-affected storage units.
Report the deviation and associated adverse reaction to the IRB and sponsor on an expedited basis per applicable timelines, and document root cause and corrective actions in the site's deviation log.
memo.responsible_party: Site 105 Principal Investigator, in coordination with the Sponsor's Safety/Regulatory Affairs team
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 calendar days of this memo, given the subject safety impact and expedited reporting requirement

memo.summary: Site 106 obtained informed consent from Subject 106-9006 using outdated ICF v2.1 rather than the approved v4.0 (effective 2024-03-01), resulting in the subject not being informed of a material new safety warning regarding a significant drug interaction between the investigational product and commonly co-prescribed anticoagulants prior to dosing.
memo.root_cause_narrative: Investigator findings confirm this is a substantive informed consent violation involving omission of material safety information, not a minor administrative/version-control lapse. The site's consent tracking process failed to ensure the current approved ICF version was in use at the time of enrollment, and the subject was dosed without being informed of an emerging safety risk that could have affected their willingness to participate. The classifier and adjudicator both categorized this as major with high confidence (0.93) and no override was applied, consistent with the material_safety_change=true determination. This indicates a breakdown in the site's version-control and document-management process for consent forms rather than an isolated clerical error.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation definition per ICH E3(R1). Consent v4.0 (effective 2024-03-01) introduced a material safety change per get_consent_version_in_effect for EVL-2024-106 on 2024-07-06. Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Re-consent Subject 106-9006 immediately using current approved ICF v4.0, ensuring the new anticoagulant drug-interaction warning is explicitly reviewed and documented, and assess whether the subject is currently on any co-prescribed anticoagulants requiring clinical follow-up.

Retrain Site 106 coordination and PI staff specifically on the site's consent version control procedure, including how to verify the currently effective IRB-approved ICF version before each consent visit.
Conduct a site-level audit of all subjects consented at Site 106 since v4.0's 2024-03-01 effective date to identify any other subjects who may have been consented on outdated versions.

Implement a mandatory pre-dosing checkpoint requiring a second-person verification (e.g., regulatory coordinator sign-off) confirming the ICF version in use matches the current IRB-approved version, logged in the site regulatory binder.
Report this deviation to the IRB and sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs team on an expedited basis given the material safety omission.
memo.responsible_party: Site 106 Principal Investigator, in coordination with Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs

memo.summary: Subject 107-9007's Visit 3 (Week 8) was conducted 4 days outside the protocol-specified visit window. No safety assessments were affected. Classification as a minor/not-important protocol deviation was confirmed on adjudication (no override).
memo.root_cause_narrative: The visit window overage appears attributable to site-level scheduling logistics rather than any safety or data-integrity concern; no safety assessments were impacted by the timing shift. The classifier's initial categorization of 'minor' was upheld on adjudication with high confidence (0.85), and no site-history pattern of recurring visit-window deviations was identified in the materials provided for this subject or site.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but should still be logged and trended.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the 4-day visit window overage for Subject 107-9007, Visit 3 (Week 8), in the site deviation log with explicit no-safety-impact rationale.
Have the site coordinator confirm and record that no protocol-specified safety assessments were due or missed as a result of the timing shift.
Add this deviation to the site's visit-window deviation tracker to monitor for recurrence at this site over the next 2-3 subject visits.
Reinforce visit scheduling procedures with site staff (e.g., calendar reminders/tickler system for upcoming visit windows) to reduce risk of future window overages.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator / Site Clinical Research Coordinator (Site Quality to confirm)
memo.target_resolution_date: 30 days from adjudication date (to be confirmed by Site Quality/Clinical Operations)

memo.summary: Subject 108-9008 failed to complete the non-critical symptom diary at Visit 4 (Week 12). The item is not linked to primary endpoints and has been classified as a minor/not-important protocol deviation, consistent with the classifier's initial categorization.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation arose from an omission in administering or collecting the non-critical symptom diary at the Week 12 visit. No override of the classifier's 'minor' categorization occurred (confidence 0.9), and no site-history pattern has been flagged in the adjudication findings provided. This appears to be an isolated administrative miss with no bearing on primary endpoint data integrity or subject safety.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but should still be logged and trended.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the missed non-critical symptom diary for Subject 108-9008 at Visit 4 (Week 12) in the site deviation log, including rationale confirming no impact on primary endpoints.
Site coordinator to verify with source records whether the diary can still be administered retrospectively or must be marked as permanently missed, and note the outcome in the file.

Add this deviation to the site-level deviation trending log specifically for non-critical diary/questionnaire omissions to confirm this remains an isolated event rather than a recurring pattern at this site.
Reinforce visit-completion checklist procedures with site staff to ensure non-critical diary items are collected at each scheduled visit going forward.
Assign a named individual to close out this log entry once documentation and trending review are complete.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator / Site Clinical Research Coordinator (Site Quality to confirm)

memo.summary: Subject 109-9009 administered a dose of Study Drug RN-88 approximately 2 hours after the scheduled time. No corrective action was taken at the time of the event. Classified as a minor (not-important) protocol deviation.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation resulted from a delay in dosing administration relative to the protocol-specified schedule. There is no indication of subject harm or data integrity impact given the limited 2-hour window. The classifier's initial category of 'minor' was confirmed on adjudication with no override, and no site-history pattern was flagged in the materials provided. This appears to be an isolated timing deviation requiring documentation and trending rather than immediate corrective intervention.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but should still be logged and trended.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the dosing delay and no-impact rationale (2-hour window, no expected effect on RN-88 pharmacokinetics/safety) in the subject's site file
Assign a named site coordinator to close out the deviation log entry within the standard site quality review cycle

Add this event to the site-level deviation trending log specifically tracking dosing-time deviations for subject 109-9009 and site 109 to confirm this remains isolated and does not recur for this subject or others at the site
Provide a brief reminder/retraining to site staff on dosing window adherence and timely reporting of deviations at time of occurrence
memo.responsible_party: Site Clinical Coordinator / Site Quality Lead (109)

memo.summary: Subject 110-9010 had vital signs at Visit 2 (Week 4) recorded using a backup manual cuff instead of the automated device, in accordance with site backup procedure. Classified as a minor/not-important protocol deviation with no expected impact on subject safety or data integrity.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation occurred because the automated vital signs device was unavailable or non-functional at the time of the Visit 2 assessment, prompting site staff to follow their approved backup procedure of using a manual cuff. This reflects appropriate contingency use rather than a procedural failure, and no override of the classifier's minor categorization was applied (classifier and adjudicator both concurred at minor, confidence 0.6). No site-history pattern of repeated device or equipment-related deviations has been identified in the information provided, though this should be confirmed through trending.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but should be logged and trended.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the deviation in the site file, including confirmation that the manual cuff reading was obtained per approved backup procedure and rationale for no impact on subject safety or endpoint data.
Verify the automated device's operational status post-visit and log any maintenance or replacement actions taken.
Add this event to the site's equipment-deviation trending log to confirm whether backup-cuff use at this site remains an isolated occurrence or begins to recur across subjects/visits.
Confirm the site's written backup vital-signs procedure is current, accessible, and was followed correctly in this instance.
Assign a named site quality/clinical operations staff member to close out the log entry once documentation is complete.
memo.responsible_party: Site Quality / Clinical Operations Lead (site-level, e.g., Site Coordinator or Site Quality Manager)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of deviation identification

memo.summary: Subject 111-9011 had an exploratory, non-primary biomarker sample collected 3 days outside the protocol-specified window. No primary or safety endpoint data was affected. Classified as minor (not-important) protocol deviation; classification confirmed on adjudication with no override.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation resulted from a scheduling/logistics lapse in coordinating the exploratory biomarker collection visit within the specified window. The classifier's initial 'minor' categorization was confirmed by adjudication (confidence 0.86) with no override, and no site-history pattern of similar deviations has been identified in the materials provided; this appears to be an isolated scheduling miss rather than a systemic site issue.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but should still be logged and trended.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the 3-day window excursion for the exploratory biomarker sample and the no-impact rationale (non-primary/non-safety endpoint) in Subject 111-9011's site file

Verify and document that the exploratory biomarker assay result remains scientifically valid/usable despite the timing deviation, or flag for exclusion if the sponsor's analytical plan requires strict windowing
Log the deviation in the site deviation tracking log with a named individual accountable for closure sign-off
Review site scheduling procedures for exploratory/non-critical sample collections to identify whether calendar reminders or visit-window alerts need reinforcement
Include this deviation in the site's periodic deviation trend review to confirm it remains an isolated event and not an emerging pattern for this site or study coordinator
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator / Site Clinical Research Coordinator (Site Quality lead to confirm)
memo.target_resolution_date: 30 days from deviation identification date (recommend confirming exact date with site quality lead)

memo.summary: Subject 112-9012 received verbal, rather than written, dietary instructions prior to their Screening Visit. The deviation is classified as minor/not-important, with no impact on assessment validity or subject safety.
memo.root_cause_narrative: Site staff communicated pre-visit dietary preparation instructions to the subject verbally instead of using the required written instruction document. This appears to be an isolated process lapse in adherence to the standard instructional method rather than a failure that affected the reliability of screening assessment data. The classifier's initial category (minor) was retained on adjudication with no override, indicating no disagreement between automated and human-reviewed classification. No site-history pattern has been identified in the materials provided; this should be confirmed through trending review rather than assumed.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but must be logged and trended per site quality procedures.
recommended_capa_actions: Document in the site file the specific dietary instructions that were verbally conveyed to Subject 112-9012 and the rationale supporting a no-impact determination on screening assessment validity.
Retrain the coordinator(s) involved in this subject's screening visit on the requirement to provide written (not verbal) dietary instructions ahead of Screening Visits, with signed acknowledgment.

Add this deviation to the site's deviation log and cross-check against prior entries at this site for verbal-vs-written instruction lapses to confirm the event remains isolated and does not indicate an emerging pattern.
Perform a spot-check on the next 2-3 scheduled screening visits at this site to confirm written dietary instructions are being properly issued going forward.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator / Site Quality Coordinator (to confirm)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of deviation identification (recommend confirming exact date with site quality lead)

adjudication.override_reason: The deviation text states the incorrect kit assignment was actually dispensed to Subject 113-9013 (i.e., reached the subject), which per the technical-vs-major boundary note means a technical system failure escalates to major once it actually reaches and affects a subject, rather than remaining a consequence-free technical/systems issue.

memo.summary: An IVRS system outage at Site 113 led to Subject 113-9013 being dispensed an incorrect study kit assignment. Initially classified as a technical/systems deviation, the category was overridden to major because the erroneous assignment actually reached and affected the subject rather than being caught before dispensing.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The IVRS outage prevented the system from providing correct real-time kit assignment guidance at the point of dispensing. Site staff proceeded with dispensing without a manual verification fallback, resulting in Subject 113-9013 receiving an incorrect study kit. The classifier initially scored this as a technical/systems issue based on the underlying cause (system outage), but adjudication overrode this to major because the failure was not contained internally—it propagated to actual subject impact, meeting the threshold where a technical failure that reaches a subject is treated as a major deviation rather than a consequence-free systems issue. This escalation should be explicitly noted in site training materials, as reliance on IVRS availability without a manual backup verification step represents a systemic gap, not a one-off error.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); base deviation definition per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain Site 113 dispensing staff specifically on the manual kit-verification and IVRS-downtime contingency procedure, emphasizing that dispensing must not proceed without confirmed correct kit assignment when the system is unavailable

Conduct clinical and safety reassessment of Subject 113-9013 to determine any impact from receiving the incorrect kit, including review of kit contents/formulation versus intended assignment and any required corrective dosing or monitoring

Implement an added monitoring checkpoint requiring a second-person manual verification of kit assignment against the randomization/dispensing log during any IVRS outage, before a kit is released to a subject

Establish an automated or manual outage-alert protocol notifying site coordinators and the sponsor's clinical monitor in real time when IVRS goes down, triggering a hold on dispensing until manual verification is confirmed
Review Site 113's history for prior IVRS-related deviations to determine whether this reflects a recurring site-level pattern requiring broader corrective action beyond this isolated event
memo.responsible_party: Site 113 Principal Investigator, in coordination with the Sponsor's Safety/Regulatory Affairs team and Clinical Monitor
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of memo issuance, pending human reviewer confirmation

memo.summary: ePRO device malfunction at Visit 3 (Week 8) for Subject 114-9014 resulted in loss of patient-reported outcome data for that visit. Classified as a technical deviation; classification was not overridden and no site-history pattern was noted in the materials provided.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation stems from a malfunction of the ePRO device used to capture patient-reported outcomes at Visit 3. The malfunction directly caused loss of PRO data for that visit for the affected subject. No information was provided indicating this is part of a recurring site-specific pattern or that the classifier's initial category was overridden; the adjudicator confirmed 'technical' with high confidence (0.92).
memo.regulatory_citation: Root-cause sub-type classification (technical) per internal CAPA taxonomy; not an official FDA/ICH category. Per guidance, this would escalate to the major reporting pathway only if the underlying equipment failure is shown to have reached/affected the subject beyond data loss (e.g., safety impact).
recommended_capa_actions: Conduct a technical root-cause investigation of the specific ePRO device/unit used by Subject 114-9014 at Visit 3, including device logs, error codes, and battery/connectivity status at time of failure.
Confirm and document whether the data loss was limited to Visit 3 PRO entries only, with no impact on other visits, other data streams, or subject safety, before closing this as technical-only.

Determine whether the missing Visit 3 PRO data can be partially recovered (e.g., device cache, cloud sync logs) or must be documented as permanently missing, and assess impact on the study endpoint/analysis plan.

Implement an added monitoring checkpoint, such as an automated device-health alert or a site-coordinator device-check step immediately before/after each PRO administration, to catch similar malfunctions before or immediately after they occur.
If the same device model or unit has a known defect, coordinate with the ePRO vendor for device replacement/firmware update and verify no other active subjects are using an affected unit.
Document the corrective action and verification steps in the site's deviation log and communicate findings to the sponsor's clinical operations and data management teams.
memo.responsible_party: Site IT/Clinical Coordinator in collaboration with the ePRO vendor's technical support and study Data Management team (to be confirmed by Quality)
memo.target_resolution_date: 30 calendar days from report date (to be confirmed by Quality)

memo.summary: At Site 115, a routine equipment maintenance audit identified that laboratory equipment used for sample analysis had exceeded its scheduled calibration service date. The lapse was discovered proactively via audit rather than through a data quality issue.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation stems from a breakdown in the site's calibration tracking process, resulting in the equipment's service date being missed without triggering a timely alert or corrective action. The classifier's initial category (technical) was confirmed by adjudication with no override, and no site-history pattern of recurring calibration lapses was noted in the materials provided. The root cause appears to be an administrative/process gap in calibration scheduling and tracking rather than equipment malfunction itself.
memo.regulatory_citation: Root-cause sub-type (technical) per internal CAPA labeling framework; not an official FDA/ICH category. Escalation to a major reporting pathway would apply only if analysis confirms the calibration lapse affected subject samples or data.
recommended_capa_actions: Conduct a root-cause investigation into why the calibration service date was missed, including review of the site's calibration tracking log/system and any responsible staff notifications.

Review all sample analyses run on the affected equipment since its last valid calibration to determine whether any subject data or samples were impacted; document findings before closing as technical-only.
Perform an out-of-tolerance assessment on the equipment to confirm whether readings during the lapsed period were within acceptable range.
Implement an automated calibration due-date alert (e.g., electronic reminder or facilities management system flag) with escalation to site QA if the deadline is not met.
Add a redundant secondary check (e.g., quarterly cross-check by a second staff member or QA sign-off) on calibration status for lab equipment at Site 115.
Retrain Site 115 lab and facilities staff on calibration scheduling procedures and documentation requirements.
memo.responsible_party: Site 115 Quality/Facilities Manager, in coordination with Sponsor Quality Systems team
memo.target_resolution_date: 30 days from report date, pending confirmation of impact assessment findings

memo.summary: An EDC system outage at Site 116 delayed timely entry of visit data for Subject 116-9016 beyond the protocol-specified window. Classified as a technical deviation with no override or site-history pattern noted.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation resulted from an EDC system outage at Site 116 that prevented site staff from entering Subject 116-9016's visit data within the required protocol window. This is a system/infrastructure failure rather than a site staff error or protocol misunderstanding. Classification as 'technical' was confirmed by adjudication (not overridden; classifier and final category match, confidence 0.87). No site-history pattern of recurring technical deviations was indicated in the materials provided.
memo.regulatory_citation: Root-cause sub-type, not an official FDA/ICH category (see data/labels.md Regulatory basis). Would escalate to the major pathway only if the underlying system failure is shown to have reached a subject (e.g., data loss, missed safety assessment, or compromised subject decision-making).
recommended_capa_actions: Investigate and document the root cause of the EDC outage (e.g., server/hosting failure, network issue, vendor-side maintenance lapse) affecting Site 116, including outage start/end time and scope of affected users.

Confirm and document that Subject 116-9016's visit data was ultimately entered accurately and completely, and that no clinical or safety data was lost, altered, or unavailable to the site/sponsor during the outage.
Verify whether any other subjects or visits at Site 116 were affected by the same outage window and reconcile their data entry status.

Implement an automated outage/downtime alert (e.g., system status monitoring or EDC vendor notification protocol) to notify site coordinators and IT immediately upon detection of an outage, enabling faster escalation and manual backup documentation procedures.
Establish a documented manual/paper backup data capture procedure for use during future EDC downtime, with a defined timeline for back-entry into EDC once restored.
Confirm with the EDC vendor whether service-level agreements (SLAs) for uptime were met and request a formal outage report/root-cause statement from the vendor.
memo.responsible_party: Site 116 IT/EDC support lead, in coordination with Sponsor Quality Systems and the EDC vendor's technical support team (to be confirmed by QA reviewer)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of memo issuance, pending confirmation by the quality reviewer

memo.summary: A temperature excursion occurred in the storage freezer at Site 117. The automated alarm detected the excursion before any dose was dispensed. Affected stock was immediately quarantined and no subject received out-of-spec product. Classified as a technical/equipment deviation with no subject impact confirmed.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation stems from an equipment/system failure in the freezer's temperature control, resulting in a storage temperature excursion. The existing automated alarm functioned as intended, detecting the excursion prior to dispensing and allowing timely quarantine of affected stock. No override of the classifier's initial category occurred (classifier and adjudicated category both technical, confidence 0.92), and no site-history pattern of recurring excursions was noted in the materials provided. The root cause of the underlying freezer malfunction itself (e.g., mechanical failure, door seal, compressor issue, power fluctuation) has not yet been determined and requires investigation to prevent recurrence.
memo.regulatory_citation: Root-cause sub-type classification (technical) per internal CAPA taxonomy; not an official FDA/ICH category. Per guidance, this remains on the minor/technical pathway unless investigation shows the underlying failure reached a subject, in which case escalation to the major reporting pathway would be required.
recommended_capa_actions: Perform a root-cause investigation of the freezer unit and associated monitoring system at Site 117 to identify the specific mechanical, electrical, or procedural cause of the excursion.
Confirm and document via the quarantine log and drug accountability records that no subject received product from the affected lot, closing out the 'no subject impact' verification element.
Inspect and, if warranted, service or replace the freezer unit's temperature control components; verify calibration of the temperature sensor tied to the alarm system.

memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but must be logged and trended.
recommended_capa_actions: Document this deviation and its no-impact rationale in the subject's site file, explicitly cross-referencing the two prior similar scheduling-related deviations
Escalate to Site Quality/Clinical Operations as a recurring pattern rather than a standalone minor deviation, given three occurrences with identical root cause

Conduct a root-cause review of the dosing clinic's scheduling/booking process (e.g., appointment reminder system, staff handoff procedures, calendar conflicts) to identify the systemic driver of repeated ~3-hour delays
Implement a corrective process at the dosing clinic (e.g., dedicated dosing time-slot confirmation calls or automated scheduling alerts) to prevent further occurrences
Add this site's dosing-delay deviations to the site trending log with a defined threshold for further escalation (e.g., to sponsor or IRB) if a fourth occurrence happens
Assign a named individual to confirm closure of this log entry and to track resolution of the systemic scheduling issue
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator / Site Quality Lead, Clinical Operations
memo.target_resolution_date: 30 days from report date
